thread:
sara (support): FYI customer reports /v1/rerank batch call producing misaligned scores when they send multiple queries in one payload. top-1 is wrong for ~20% of requests. request_id=rid_0a9f, example attached below.

frank (cust): the top results are from other queries, so ranking is useless. this started after we moved to batch mode. noticed with >1 query.

sara (support): Repro payload (sanitized):
```json
{
  "queries": [
    { "query_id": "q1", "text": "how to reset password" },
    { "query_id": "q2", "text": "change subscription" }
  ],
  "candidates": [
    [ {"id": "a1"}, {"id": "a2"}, {"id": "a3"} ],
    [ {"id": "b1"}, {"id": "b2"} ]
  ]
}
```
Response we see (simplified):
```json
{ "scores": [0.91, 0.87, 0.02, 0.78, 0.65], "ranked_ids": ["a1","a2","b1","a3","b2"] }
```
But in many requests the first 3 scores were applied to q2's candidates, i.e. shifted.

diego (eng-ml): thanks, digging in. earliest hypothesis: mapper that flattens candidate lists then reconstructs per-query offsets may be using a stale counter when arrays are empty/short. can you also paste the raw curl and headers (content-type + any custom rerank headers)?

sara (support): curl below (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer [redacted]' -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' -d '@payload.json'
```
header looks normal. We do see this more when payloads are large (20+ queries) but also hit with 2 queries occasionally.

liam (eng-runtime): tagging in. I'm seeing flaky behavior in the streaming/chunked reader when a client omits Content-Length and the runtime falls back to chunked parsing. boundary indices were computed from a running index into the flattened candidate vector; if a zero-length candidate array appears, index arithmetic was off-by-one. probable root cause.

liam (eng-runtime): quick workaround for customers: include explicit "candidate_counts" top-level array with counts per query, e.g. "candidate_counts": [3,2]. server will use that when present to reconstruct boundaries deterministically. also try sending Content-Length to avoid chunked path.

frank (cust): can you confirm this won't change billing? we pay per candidate token output — worried about overcharging if responses are adjusted.

pm (product): short answer: no billing differences expected for a reconstruction-only fix; we'll confirm. tagging finance for a follow-up.

diego (eng-ml): I created a small repro harness and ran the exact payload. got the misalignment locally with chunked parser enabled. with candidate_counts provided, results stable.

diego (eng-ml): repro steps for eng:
1) payload.json as above with nested candidates arrays
2) send with header "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" (curl -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" --data-binary @payload.json)
3) inspect response.ranked_ids and map to queries by summing candidate lengths

qa (eng): I'll write a regression that fuzzes empty/variable-length candidate arrays and validates alignment invariants: sum(candidate_counts) == len(scores) and every query gets contiguous slice.

liam (eng-runtime): plan: patch parser to always consult explicit candidate_counts and to add sanity-check guards when reconstructing offsets. we'll ship a canary tomorrow to 10% of hosts.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427 - multiquery rerank boundary misalignment. Link: https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-2026-0427

sara (support): customer update queued. advising immediate workaround (candidate_counts + Content-Length). will offer canary opt-in if needed.

liam (eng-runtime): also note a short-term header to enable strict parsing: X-Rerank-Strict: true — defaults to false. we'll honor it in canary so support can ask customers to opt-in per the workaround.

diego (eng-ml): logging note: when you paste rid (rid_0a9f) in the support case I'll pull the trace (trace=0x7d3f2) and attach logs. saw stack frames in mapper: flattenCandidates -> reconstructOffsets -> offByOne when candidate.length == 0.

sara (support): thanks. I'll push the workaround to Frank and ask for a repro sample if they see it again. will attach the incident ticket and proposed timeline. :+1:

liam (eng-runtime): follow-ups: hotfix + regression + canary rollout. ETA for canary start: tomorrow 0900 UTC. full rollout after validation: +48h.

pm (product): add to release notes and customer-facing KB: "Rerank batching: recommended payload fields (candidate_counts)".

frank (cust): appreciated — we'll try candidate_counts and report back. thanks for the quick turnaround.

sara (support): closing loop here once canary is green or if customer reports continued issues.
